question: How many guards are in the system?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS guard_count FROM guards
notes: Simple count; no status interpretation.

question: Show guard names and emails.
sql: SELECT first_name, last_name, email FROM guards ORDER BY id LIMIT 20
notes: Return only requested names and emails; id supports ordering without being displayed. Blocked fields remain excluded.

question: List all sites.
sql: SELECT site FROM sites ORDER BY id LIMIT 20
notes: A broad list request returns the identifying name, not every field. Additional allowed details can be requested.

question: Find customers whose name contains Security.
sql: SELECT customer FROM customers WHERE LOWER(customer) LIKE '%security%' ORDER BY id LIMIT 20
notes: Return matching customer names without adding unrequested contact details or status.

question: How many users are there for each role?
sql: SELECT role_type, COUNT(*) AS user_count FROM users GROUP BY role_type ORDER BY user_count DESC LIMIT 20
notes: Aggregation example.

question: List scheduled shifts ordered by start time.
sql: SELECT id, shift_code, start_at, end_at, status FROM shifts WHERE status = 'scheduled' ORDER BY start_at LIMIT 100
notes: Uses a declared enum and returns identifiers without guessing joins.

question: How many attendance records are there for each status?
sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count FROM attendance GROUP BY status ORDER BY attendance_count DESC LIMIT 100
notes: Reports recorded status literals.

question: List open high or critical severity incidents.
sql: SELECT id, incident_code, title, severity, status, created_at FROM incidents WHERE status = 'open' AND severity IN ('high', 'critical') ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100
notes: Uses declared enums.

question: List overdue customer invoices.
sql: SELECT id, invoice_number, customer_id, total_amount, status FROM invoices WHERE status = 'overdue' ORDER BY id LIMIT 100
notes: Customer invoices, not supplier invoices; currency is unspecified.

question: List compliance expiry dates and statuses.
sql: SELECT guard_id, sia_expiry_date, sia_status, rtw_expiry_date, rtw_status FROM guard_compliance ORDER BY guard_id LIMIT 100
notes: Excludes document numbers and private notes.

question: List sites with their customer names.
sql: SELECT s.id, s.site, c.customer FROM sites s LEFT JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY s.id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Show contracts with their site and customer names.
sql: SELECT cc.id, cc.contract_title, s.site, c.customer FROM client_contracts cc LEFT JOIN sites s ON cc.site_id = s.id LEFT JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY cc.id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Count sites for every customer, including customers with no sites.
sql: SELECT c.id, c.customer, COUNT(s.id) AS site_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sites s ON s.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.customer ORDER BY c.id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Show attendance records with guard names and shift start times.
sql: SELECT a.id, g.first_name, g.last_name, s.start_at, a.status FROM attendance a LEFT JOIN guards g ON a.guard_id = g.id LEFT JOIN shifts s ON a.shift_id = s.id ORDER BY a.id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Show shift assignments with shift codes and guard names.
sql: SELECT a.id, s.shift_code, g.first_name, g.last_name FROM shift_assignments a JOIN shifts s ON a.shift_id = s.id JOIN guards g ON a.guard_id = g.id ORDER BY a.id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Show incidents with the reporting guard names.
sql: SELECT i.id, i.title, g.first_name, g.last_name FROM incidents i LEFT JOIN guards g ON i.reported_by_guard_id = g.id ORDER BY i.id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Show guard requests with requester and target guard names.
sql: SELECT r.id, requester.first_name AS requester_first_name, requester.last_name AS requester_last_name, target.first_name AS target_first_name, target.last_name AS target_last_name, r.status FROM guard_requests r LEFT JOIN guards requester ON r.guard_id = requester.id LEFT JOIN guards target ON r.target_guard_id = target.id ORDER BY r.id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Show supplier invoices with supplier names and purchase order numbers.
sql: SELECT i.id, i.invoice_number, s.supplier, p.po_number, i.amount FROM supplier_invoices i LEFT JOIN suppliers s ON i.supplier_id = s.id LEFT JOIN purchase_orders p ON i.purchase_order_id = p.id ORDER BY i.id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Show system user names and their linked guard names.
sql: SELECT u.user_id, u.name, g.first_name, g.last_name FROM users u LEFT JOIN guards g ON u.guard_id = g.id ORDER BY u.user_id LIMIT 100
notes: Uses owner-confirmed business_schema relationships, explicit safe columns and role aliases; no database foreign keys required.

question: Show unassigned shifts.
sql: SELECT s.id, s.shift_code, s.start_at, s.end_at FROM shifts s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shift_assignments a WHERE a.shift_id = s.id) ORDER BY s.start_at LIMIT 100

question: Show all sites assigned to guard with first name Ali.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT st.id, st.site, st.site_code FROM guards g JOIN shift_assignments a ON a.guard_id = g.id JOIN shifts s ON a.shift_id = s.id JOIN sites st ON s.site_id = st.id WHERE LOWER(g.first_name) = 'ali' ORDER BY st.site LIMIT 100

question: Show recorded guard availability windows starting on 2026-09-25.
sql: SELECT id, guard_id, day_of_week, start_at, end_at, status FROM guard_availabilities WHERE start_at >= '2026-09-25 00:00:00' AND start_at < '2026-09-26 00:00:00' ORDER BY start_at, id LIMIT 20
notes: Uses full DATETIME boundaries; displays recorded status without assuming shift-conflict checks or recurring weekly availability.
